question_text: Draw a series RLC Band-Pass filter. What does its Bode plot look like, and what is its primary application?
answer_text: An inductor, capacitor, and resistor all in series. The Bode plot looks like a mountain peak (a bell curve). It is used to tune into a specific frequency while blocking all others.
explanation_text: To create a band-pass, you measure the output voltage strictly across the resistor. At low frequencies, the capacitor acts like an open circuit and blocks the signal (+20dB/dec slope upward). At high frequencies, the inductor blocks the signal (-20dB/dec slope downward). But at exactly the resonant frequency (f_0 = 1 / (2π√LC)), the inductive and capacitive reactances perfectly cancel each other out (X_L = X_C), leaving only the resistor. The signal passes through unattenuated (0 dB) only at this "peak."
bonus_question_text: What determines the "bandwidth" (how wide the mountain peak is) of this series RLC filter?
bonus_answer_text: The resistor value. A smaller resistor results in less damping and a higher "Q-factor" (a sharper, narrower peak). A larger resistor dampens the resonance, creating a wider bandwidth.
